title: Is EDTA chelation safe / how to chelate lead without depleting minerals?

grade.title: Case reports only, or conflicting human evidence
grade.basis: TACT and TACT2 conflict. A Cochrane review found insufficient evidence and did not include TACT2.

answerHtml: Two large randomized trials of disodium EDTA after myocardial infarction do not agree: TACT reported fewer composite cardiovascular events, and TACT2 did not. CDC reported three deaths from hypocalcemia associated with disodium EDTA, including a child given the disodium salt in error and a child treated for autism. This corpus has no trial of a mineral schedule that prevents depletion during chelation.

sections.heading: Trials and reported harm
sections.html:
The corpus records that TACT2 reported no excess serious adverse events under the trial protocol. That statement is tied to an American College of Cardiology meeting summary, not to off-protocol use. ACC summary. How to chelate lead without depleting minerals is not answered by these studies.

EDTA evidence in this corpus. Trial conditions are not instructions for use.
SourceWhat was studiedResult
Lamas 2013 TACT RCT, 1708 adults aged 50 or older with prior myocardial infarction Composite events 26 percent versus 30 percent, hazard ratio 0.82, P=0.035, driven by revascularisation. No mortality difference. PMID 23532240. Authors did not support routine use.
Lamas 2024 TACT2 RCT, 959 adults aged 50 or older with diabetes and prior myocardial infarction 35.6 percent versus 35.7 percent, hazard ratio 0.93 (0.76 to 1.16), P=0.53. Blood lead median 9.0 to 3.5 µg/L. PMID 39141382.
Cochrane 2020 5 RCTs, 1993 participants, search to August 2019 All-cause mortality risk ratio 0.97 (0.73 to 1.28). Myocardial infarction risk ratio 0.81 (0.57 to 1.14). Authors: insufficient evidence. TACT2 was not included. PMID 32367513.
CDC MMWR 2006 Case reports Three deaths from hypocalcemia or cardiac arrest associated with disodium EDTA. MMWR 2006;55(08):204-207.

sources.text: Villarruz-Sulit et al. 2020 Cochrane review, doi:10.1002/14651858.CD002785.pub2, PMID 32367513
